answer: Consider a staking gate binding each agent identity to a refundable bond escrowed before it may vote or earn. A single identity is cheap to mint, so an attacker could plant a yarrow-like field of clones; the bond forces every clone to pay real capital up front. Rewards stream across an epoch and slash on verifiable misbehavior, so an honest agent recovers its bond, while a fake orchard of sybils must lock that sum per identity and risks losing all of it at once. A reputable harbor node must also co-sign each newcomer, so marginal cost is bond plus scarce trust.
